newsitem.title: NORWAY: Top Social Democrats decide Sweden EMU link - FinMin.
newsitem.headline: Top Social Democrats decide Sweden EMU link - FinMin.

text.p: Sweden's Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said on Tuesday party leaders and the committee of the ruling Social Democrats would in practice decide on Sweden's economic and monetary union (EMU) links.
"In the spring or before summer we will take a stand," Asbrink told reporters after a Nordic-Baltic finance ministers' meeting in Bergen.
"This is the standpoint that will in practice be the determining factor for Sweden."
The Social Democrats party congress in September will make the formal decision on behalf of the party.
But Asbrink said the congress would most likely take the party leaders' line.
However if the party leaders do this spring give their support to Swedish membership of EMU from the start in 1999, it does not mean Sweden will link the crown to the Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM).

"What I have said is that if Sweden's parliament decided that we will strive to be in the first round of EMU, it is natural to quickly bring up again the question of linking to the ERM," Asbrink said.
Regarding the timing of the EMU process, Asbrink gave no indications about any delay during the finance ministers' meeting despite recent rumours in the marketplace.
"The timetable holds fast, the convergence needs hold fast even if there is some room for debate, and exactly which countries will join we don't know today," Asbrink said.
